topics.label: Generalization in overparameterized networks
topics.summary: Classical puzzles about why heavily overparameterized deep networks generalize at all, which frame both scaling and grokking.

claims.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
claims.rationale: Shows networks can memorize random labels yet generalize on real data, establishing that capacity-based bounds cannot explain generalization; the starting puzzle for everything downstream.

claims.title: Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt
claims.rationale: Documents double descent in model size, data and training time; the epoch-wise form is the closest classical relative of grokking and motivates thinking about generalization as a function of scale.

topics.label: Scaling laws and emergent abilities
topics.summary: How loss and capabilities change predictably (or apparently discontinuously) with compute, parameters and data.

claims.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
claims.rationale: The original power-law fits of language-model loss against parameters, data and compute; defines the vocabulary used by all later scaling work.

claims.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
claims.rationale: The Chinchilla paper: revises Kaplan's conclusions by showing data and parameters should scale together, and shows how sensitive scaling-law conclusions are to methodology.

claims.title: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models
claims.rationale: Catalogues abilities that appear abruptly at scale despite smooth loss curves, raising the question of whether generalization is predictable from scaling laws.

claims.title: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?
claims.rationale: Argues emergence is largely an artifact of discontinuous metrics; read against Wei et al. to see how metric choice shapes claims about generalization.

topics.label: Grokking and delayed generalization
topics.summary: Networks that memorize first and generalize much later, and the mechanistic accounts of why.

claims.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
claims.rationale: Introduces the grokking phenomenon on modular arithmetic: validation accuracy jumps long after training accuracy saturates, with weight decay as a key lever.

claims.title: Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability
claims.rationale: Reverse-engineers the Fourier-based algorithm a grokked transformer learns and shows the generalizing circuit forms gradually, making the phase transition measurable before it is visible.

claims.title: Omnigrok: Grokking Beyond Algorithmic Data
claims.rationale: Explains grokking through weight norm and the loss landscape, and induces it on images and text, showing it is a general training dynamic rather than a toy curiosity.

topics.label: Calibration and models knowing what they know
topics.summary: Whether a model's confidence tracks its correctness, and whether it has internal access to its own knowledge.

claims.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
claims.rationale: Defines the modern calibration toolkit (reliability diagrams, ECE, temperature scaling) and shows that deeper networks became worse calibrated; the baseline all LM calibration work cites.

claims.title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
claims.rationale: Shows large LMs are well calibrated on multiple choice and can predict P(True) and P(IK) for their own answers, with self-knowledge improving with scale; ties calibration directly to scaling.

claims.title: Teaching Models to Express Their Uncertainty in Words
claims.rationale: Fine-tunes GPT-3 to state verbal confidence that is calibrated and survives distribution shift, distinguishing verbalized from logit-based calibration.

claims.title: Discovering Latent Knowledge in Language Models Without Supervision
claims.rationale: Finds a truth direction in activations without labels (CCS), suggesting models encode what they know separately from what they say; bridges calibration and latent representations.

topics.label: Latent and chain-of-thought reasoning
topics.summary: How reasoning is carried out in tokens versus hidden states, whether stated reasoning is faithful, and how implicit reasoning relates to grokking.

claims.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
claims.rationale: Establishes that externalizing intermediate steps unlocks multi-step reasoning, and only at scale; the reference point for all later latent-reasoning work.

claims.title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
claims.rationale: Shows chain-of-thought can be systematically unfaithful to the factors driving the answer, so stated reasoning is not a reliable window on latent computation.

claims.title: Grokked Transformers are Implicit Reasoners: A Mechanistic Journey to the Edge of Generalization
claims.rationale: Links the two themes directly: transformers acquire implicit multi-hop reasoning only through grokking, and generalization differs by task structure (composition vs comparison).

claims.title: Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space
claims.rationale: Coconut: feeds hidden states back as reasoning steps instead of tokens, showing breadth-first-like latent search; the current frontier of reasoning without verbalization.

topic_edges.to: Calibration and models knowing what they know
